cohort: 454 women admitted for delivery from March 22 to April 18, 2020, at two New York City hospitals
finding: COVID-19 symptoms were present in a minority of COVID-19-positive women admitted for delivery, and while COVID-19 was associated with differences in obstetrical outcomes and increased risk for certain diagnoses, demographic risk factors alone were not strong predictors of COVID-19 status.
mod_finding: Women with COVID-19 were less likely to have a vaginal delivery (55.2% vs. 51.9%, p = 0.04) and had a significantly longer postpartum length of stay with cesarean (2.00 vs. 2.67days, p < 0.01).
